description: External-agent security policy (ADR-0090 external SSOT / ADR-0059 D6). The launch-side twin of protocol/agent-capabilities.json: that file says what an agent CAN do, this one says what Cognia is willing to LAUNCH. TypeScript consumes it directly; Rust keeps its own literal arrays (a compiled-in allowlist must not depend on runtime JSON parsing) and `pnpm audit:agent-capabilities` enforces that the two agree.

sandbox.note: Cognia never runs an external agent unsandboxed. A platform with neither macOS Seatbelt nor Linux bubblewrap cannot host one at all, which is a refusal to surface BEFORE the user configures an agent -- not an error at spawn time.

binaryAllowlist.note: Bare binary names an external-agent spawn may execute (no path separators). Every entry must be justified: either a shipped preset names it as `process.command`, or it appears under `manualOnly` WITH a reason. An entry that is neither is attack surface the headless spawn RPC exposes and no Cognia code path can ask for -- which is exactly what `cline` was.

manualOnly.claude: The Claude Code CLI itself. No preset spawns it (the `claude-code` preset uses the ACP adapter binary), but hand-configured agents and the container/kube backends do.
manualOnly.claude-code-acp: Zed's ACP bridge, installed globally by users who prefer it over the first-party adapter. It is also the default command in `container_backend.rs` / `kube_backend.rs`.
manualOnly.codex-acp: The Zed Codex ACP shim as a GLOBAL install; the shipped preset uses the `npx @zed-industries/codex-acp` form. `workspace_runtime_backend.rs` spawns the bare name.
manualOnly.gemini: The Gemini CLI as a global install; the shipped preset uses the `npx @google/gemini-cli` form.

agentStateWritableRoots.note: Home-relative paths each agent family must be able to write inside the sandbox. Matching runs against the RESOLVED target: for `npx <package>` that is the package, otherwise the base command with any Windows executable suffix stripped. `match` is either "contains" (substring of the target), "target" (target equals one of `values`) or "base" (the base command equals one of `values`) -- Pi needs the exact forms because "copilot" contains "pi". A missing root does not fail the launch; it silently breaks whatever the agent stores there, which is how OpenCode's absence went unnoticed while its session resume started over every time.

fileRoots.note: Roots that are FILES rather than directories; a sandbox scope naming a path that does not exist is not the same as one naming an empty file.
